findings.title: Gate workload `mid-flock-50k` is N=100,000, not N=50k, and does not match the baseline configuration
findings.description:
Line 128 makes `mid-flock-50k` the gate configuration for A2/A3 "at N=50k", and Step 3 (lines 161–175) expects it to reproduce the ~38 TPS baseline. The file as it exists does neither:

- **Wrong N:** `bench/workloads/mid-flock-50k.yaml:7` has `n: 100000`, with `world_size: [1536.0, 1536.0]`, `cluster_radius: 45.0`, flocker 1.00 / leader 0.00, four forces and no leadership.
- **Baseline was a different config:** the 38 TPS figure was measured at N=50k, world 756×756, 95/5 flocker/leader, five forces (`145-notes.fused-tick-measurements.md:28-47`). Slice 145 measured about 11 TPS at N=100k.
- **Occupancy figures came from a third config:** the p99≈5137 / "~555 at S=3" numbers come from an inline spec with `cluster_radius: 80` (`scripts/148_measure_cell_occupancy.py:61-80`).
- **No override exists:** no YAML in `bench/workloads/` reproduces the baseline, and the CLI has no N override (`src/migratory/bench/cli.py:17-55`).

As written, A2 (≥5× vs baseline) and A3 (≥100 TPS at N=50k) would be measured on a different N, density and force mix than the baseline. The design must name the exact workload: either correct this YAML or add a 50k/756×756 workload matching the baseline run.

findings.title: The S / cell_size configuration path is described against components and signatures that do not exist
findings.description:
The Component Interactions diagram and line 80 are wrong about the existing code in every hop:

- **`BenchConfig`** does not exist. Bench configuration is the frozen `Workload` dataclass (`src/migratory/bench/workload.py:99-112`), which has no `cell_size` or subdivision field.
- **"The bench harness passes `cell_size` at setup; it reads from config"** is false. `cell_size` is derived inside `GpuAgentState.setup` as `max_query_radius * DEFAULT_CELL_SIZE_MULTIPLIER` (`quadrants_fused_state.py:54,150`). The design never mentions this existing knob, which S effectively inverts.
- **`QuadrantsFusedBackend.setup()` / `tick()`**: the class is `QuadrantsFusedTickRunner` and the interface is `setup` / `tick_once` / `finalize` (`quadrants_fused_backend.py:66-150`).
- **`build_spatial_hash(cell_size=cell_size)` "computes `grid_w` and `grid_h`"**: the signature is `build_spatial_hash(state)` (`quadrants_fused_kernels.py:411`) and it computes neither. `GpuAgentState.setup` does (`quadrants_fused_state.py:151-153`).
- **No channel for S:** `run()` constructs `backend_cls()` with no arguments and calls `setup(workload)` (`src/migratory/bench/runner.py:141-150`). The design does not say whether S is a `Workload` field, a constructor argument, a CLI flag threaded through `run()`, or a second backend registration.
- **`Workload` is a costly home for it:** the loader's policy is "missing fields raise rather than defaulting silently" (`workload.py:10-11,130-136`), so a new required field touches six YAMLs and every inline `Workload.from_dict` in the tests. It is also shared with the numpy backend the design says is unchanged.
- **"Config-load time" validation (line 69)** therefore has no defined home.
- **Two kernel call sites, one shown:** adding `S` to `fused_force_integrate_kernel` must change both `run_fused_tick` (`quadrants_fused_kernels.py:400-407`) and `tick_once` (`quadrants_fused_backend.py:116-123`). The first is the path `tests/bench/test_quadrants_fused_kernels.py:102,174` exercise; missing it is an arity error at launch.
- **Multi-profile radius:** line 53's `cell_size = query_radius / S` must be `max_query_radius / S`, since the kernel reads `query_radius` per profile.

The design needs to state where S lives, who validates it, and that S is stored on `GpuAgentState` so both call sites read it. The lightest option is a `subdivision_factor=1` argument on `GpuAgentState.setup` plus one stated route from the CLI.

findings.title: Warp-divergence analysis assumes warp-mates are spatial neighbors; the code does not arrange that
findings.description:
Line 27 argues divergence is small because "threads in the same warp (agents with similar spatial index) hit the cap within a small, similar iteration window." That premise does not hold in the code:

- The parallel loop is `for i in range(n)` over agent ID (`quadrants_fused_kernels.py:233`); agents are never reordered spatially, and `sorted_agent_ids` is only an indirection (lines 111-121).
- Initial state assigns clusters round-robin by index (`numpy_backend.py:243`) with random offsets, so consecutive IDs alternate flocks and are spatially uncorrelated.
- Exit iteration depends strongly on where an agent sits in its cell (see the next finding).

A warp's cost is set by its slowest thread, so the realised saving is governed by the worst case within 32 random agents, not the mean. This puts A2 (≥5×) at risk for early exit alone. The design should either iterate in cell-sorted order (`i = _sorted_agent_ids[s]`), make exit iterations uniform via scan order, or drop the claim and treat divergence as a measured risk. My confidence in the thread-to-index mapping is good but not verified on the CUDA host.

findings.title: Interaction estimates are wrong, and the row-major scan starts at the far corner
findings.description:
- **"With S=3 alone: candidates loaded drops to ~5000" (line 58)** contradicts the source note: 49 cells × ~555 ≈ 27,000 (`148-notes.rediagnosis.md:108-110`). "With both: candidates loaded ~555" inherits the error.
- **"Exits after ~32"** assumes the first candidates visited are within radius. `range(-S, S+1)` row-major order begins at cell (−S, −S), the farthest corner, which at S=3 is wholly or mostly outside the radius. By my geometry estimate the scan before 32 acceptances runs from several hundred to roughly 3,900 candidates (a full row of 7×555), depending on the agent's position in its cell.
- **"Compose multiplicatively"** is therefore not established.
- **"Correct neighborhood is preserved" (line 56)** is true of the candidate set only. First-k selection is order-dependent, so at S=3 the accepted 32 come from the far edge of the radius disk rather than the lower-left cell.

A centre-out cell order (own cell first) would deliver the claimed ~32-candidate exit, make exit iterations uniform across a warp, and select nearer neighbors. The design should specify scan order or correct the estimates.

findings.title: Option A puts cap logic outside the seam; "A7 seam preserved" does not hold as claimed
findings.description:
- **Dead seam:** with `if k_found >= max_neighbors and max_neighbors > 0: break` ahead of the call, `get_neighbors_first_k` always returns 1 when reached. Selection now lives in the kernel body.
- **Existing test's rule is violated in substance:** `tests/bench/test_quadrants_fused_kernels.py:217-250` states the selection-of-k logic "must only appear inside `get_neighbors_first_k`". Its grep matches only `k_found < k_max` / `k_found < max_neighbors`, so the `>=` form passes by spelling. The design does not mention this test.
- **Future swap is no longer body-only:** line 112 says the swap point "remains intact", but a distance-ranked replacement must keep scanning after k candidates, so the caller's break has to be removed too. Slice 145 A7 promised the swap would not require changing the kernel structure.
- **Lighter alternative:** `148-notes.rediagnosis.md:81-82` proposed breaking when the seam returns reject, which keeps one decision site.
- **Mischaracterised history:** line 31 says the seam was the A7 swap point "for this change"; A7 is about distance-ranked selection.

The design should either adopt the break-on-reject form or state that the seam is retired and update the isolation test.

findings.title: Verification Walkthrough commands cannot run, and the four-way comparison is not expressible
findings.description:
- **No such script:** `scripts/bench.py` does not exist; `scripts/` holds only the two slice-148 scripts. The entry point is `python -m migratory.bench --workload <name> --backend <name>` (`cli.py:17-55`).
- **No such flags:** `--config`, `--N`, `--ticks`, `--subdivision-factor` and `--parity-check` do not exist. The design does not list any of them as work to add, yet lines 102-105 declare the harness and parity infrastructure unchanged.
- **Step 3 variants are indistinguishable:** the "baseline" and "early exit only" commands are identical, as are the two S=3 commands. No toggle for the break is designed, so the counter-gating variants cannot be run after the change.
- **A2's baseline has no stated source:** it should be either a pre-change run on the current commit or the recorded 25.41 ms `force_total` (`145-notes.fused-tick-measurements.md:47`).

The "draft demo script" caveat at line 139 does not cover this: the commands encode harness changes that the body of the design excludes.

findings.title: A4 parity at the gate configuration (S=3) has no test vehicle
findings.description:
- The only parity test builds the backend with `get_backend('quadrants-fused')()` and `setup(wl)` on `mid-flock`, N=3500 (`tests/bench/test_quadrants_fused_parity.py:60-94`), so it runs the default S=1.
- The design lists "Parity test infrastructure" as unchanged (line 104), while Steps 1 and 5 require S=3 parity through flags that do not exist.
- The plan's exit criterion (statistical parity within 20%) is therefore unverified for the configuration the gates run with. A parametrised S=3 case in the existing parity test would close it.
- Line 126's "Metal or CPU fallback" is also wrong: the backend has no CPU fallback (`quadrants_fused_backend.py:46-62`).

findings.title: A5 register-spill check names tools the CUDA host does not have
findings.description:
- A5 and Step 4 (line 182) cite `nvcc --ptxas-info` and `TI_PRINT_KERNEL_STATS=1 or equivalent`.
- The slice 148 notes record that `ptxas`, `cuobjdump` and `nvcc` are not installed on the CUDA host (`148-notes.envelope-measurement.md:25-27`).
- Nothing in the repo uses that environment variable; I could not confirm it exists in Quadrants.
- The established method is `strings` on the Quadrants PTX cache, counting `.local` declarations in `kernel_1_range_for` (same note, lines 29-52). The design should cite that.

findings.title: The S ≤ 8 bound rests on incorrect reasoning and duplicates an existing guard
findings.description:
- **"Larger than the physical neighborhood"** cannot be true: the scan spans (2S+1)·r/S for every S by construction.
- **"`grid_w * grid_h * cell_count` auxiliary arrays"** is not a real quantity. The auxiliary fields are three i32 arrays of `n_cells` length (`quadrants_fused_state.py:184-191`).
- **Already guarded:** `MAX_CELLS_SANITY_CAP = 4_000_000` raises `ValueError` at setup (`quadrants_fused_state.py:55,154-160`). At S=8 on a 1536 world the grid is about 60k cells.

Cut the upper bound and its rationale. Keep `S >= 1` and rely on the existing cell-count cap.

findings.title: The plan's 7-neighbor benchmark target is silently dropped
findings.description:
- The plan entry states "the 7-neighbor operating point is a benchmark target" (`140-slices.simulation-scaling.md:50`).
- The design measures only `max_neighbors=32` and lists nothing about it under Out of Scope.
- Both registry profiles hardcode `max_neighbors=32` (`workload.py:45,58`), so a 7-neighbor run needs a profile entry.

Either add one measurement at 7 or defer it explicitly.

findings.title: `break` exits only the `kk` loop; remaining cells are still visited
findings.description: After the cap, the `drow`/`dcol` loops continue, and each remaining non-empty cell costs two `_cell_start` loads plus one loop entry (49 cells at S=3). This is small in absolute terms but comparable to the ~32 accepted visits the design budgets for. A `k_found` check at cell level removes it.

findings.title: Slice 146 interface: kernel signature changes and the default leaves subdivision off
findings.description: Line 111 says only `cell_size` and inner-loop behaviour change, but `fused_force_integrate_kernel` gains a parameter that slice 146's driver will call. With default S=1, production adoption gets early exit but not subdivision unless 146 sets S. One sentence saying who chooses S for production would cover this.

findings.title: Early exit is result-identical to counter-gating at S=1
findings.description: After the cap, counter-gating accepts nothing (`quadrants_fused_kernels.py:178-184,304-306`), so breaking changes no accumulator. The `max_neighbors > 0` guard matches the uncapped encoding (`quadrants_fused_state.py:288`). The existing tests and the `n_cells=16` pin (`tests/bench/test_quadrants_fused.py:140`) are unaffected at the default. Inner-loop `break` is confirmed by the slice 145 POC on Metal (`145-notes.phase-2-risk-poc.md:17-27`).

findings.title: Code line references, problem-statement figures, NFR and dependencies check out
findings.description:
- Line 291 (`for kk`), lines 155–184 (seam) and lines 411–462 (`build_spatial_hash`) match the file.
- The 38 TPS, p99≈5000, 45,000-candidate and 99.9% figures match `148-notes.rediagnosis.md` and the 145 measurements.
- The Tier 2 NFR (60 TPS at N=50k, CUDA) is restated at line 116 with the A3 target.
- `dependencies: [145]` matches the plan entry, and the out-of-scope items match the rediagnosis note.
- The slice adds no I/O path or message type, so no failure-mode enumeration is owed.
